key_insight: The dual-term air-gap permeance (DTAP) model improves magnetic equivalent circuit accuracy by capturing both tooth-normal and tooth-tangential rotor eccentricity at comparable computational cost.
engineering_relevance: More accurate torque ripple and unbalanced magnetic pull predictions support motor fault diagnosis, control, and bearing-load assessment.
method: Use a closed-form permeance expression between stator and rotor teeth, with or without rotor skew.
Identify parameters using an air-gap FEM model containing all tooth heads to capture neighboring-tooth shielding.
Integrate DTAP into a magnetic equivalent circuit for eccentric-motor simulation.
evidence_signal: Across three motors, DTAP reduced air-gap permeance error by factors of 2.8–4.8; in an eccentric induction motor, torque ripple and peak unbalanced magnetic pull were within 1.6% and 1.3% of the reference, respectively.
watch_item: Parameter identification requires FEM, and validation across three motors does not establish accuracy for all motor geometries or eccentricity conditions.
paper_title: Improved Closed-Form Identification of the Air-Gap Permeance in Magnetic Equivalent Circuits of Rotor-Eccentric Electric Motors
